question: In ______, a dual exchange rate system called Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS) was introduced in India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun Mar 01 1992 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• The **Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS)** was introduced in India on **March 1, 1992**, as part of the broader economic reforms initiated in 1991 to address the balance of payment crisis and stabilize the Indian economy. 
• LERMS introduced a **dual exchange rate system**, where 40% of foreign exchange earnings were surrendered to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at the official exchange rate, and the remaining 60% could be converted at market-determined rates. 
• The system aimed to transition India from a fixed exchange rate regime to a more **market-driven exchange rate mechanism** in a phased manner. 
• This reform was a significant step towards integrating the Indian economy with the global market and improving the **foreign exchange reserves** of the country.
